key_insight: Gradient-aware AI agents autonomously discover turbulence closure forms and train their parameters using gradients from a differentiable CFD solver.
engineering_relevance: The framework could reduce manual closure development for turbulence simulations by jointly automating model design and a posteriori calibration.
method: Use a multi-agent LLM system to search analytical, neural, and hybrid closure forms.
Embed proposals in a GPU-native differentiable CFD solver, define objectives, and validate gradient paths.
Use truncated-horizon gradients to train parameters and guide subsequent proposals.
evidence_signal: Tests cover 2D turbulence dissipation laws and subgrid-scale closures plus 3D channel-flow wall models; gradient-based training recovers reference coefficients missed by forward evaluation within the same budget and improves agreement with targeted statistics.
watch_item: Generalization beyond the demonstrated flows remains unestablished, and implementation requires a differentiable solver with validated gradient paths.
paper_title: Gradient-Aware AI Agents for Autonomous Turbulence Model Discovery via Differentiable CFD
